checks.detail: solving dx/dt = 0 at x = 1 gives zeta_crit = C*alpha_B*chi*n_H, which is exactly 1/t_rec with t_rec of MD14 eq. (24). sympy residual 0. So the recombination-time normalisation is not a convention: it is the boundary at which ionizations can just hold the gas ionized.
checks.name: zeta t_rec >= 1 IS the steady-state maintenance condition

checks.detail: N_req - 1 = chi n_H0 alpha_B C (1+z)^(3/2) / (H0 sqrt(Omega_m)) -- linear in the clumping factor and rising as (1+z)^(3/2). sympy-verified. CONSEQUENCE: the requirement gets HARDER at higher redshift, because the gas is denser (t_rec ~ (1+z)^-3) faster than the clock is short (t_H ~ (1+z)^-3/2).
checks.name: the excess over unity scales as C (1+z)^(3/2), analytically

checks.detail: with Y_P = 0.2450 and X_H = 0.7550, singly ionized helium gives n_e/n_HII = 1 + (Y_P/4)/X_H = 1.08113, against the 1.08 quoted in MD14 eq. (24) -- agreement to 0.10%. So chi is not a fudge factor: it is the electron-per-proton ratio of a gas whose helium is singly ionized. Were helium DOUBLY ionized it would be 1 + 2(Y_P/4)/X_H = 1.16225, which is the value appropriate after HeII reionization (z < 3) and NOT here.
checks.name: chi = 1.08 DERIVED from the primordial mass fractions

checks.detail: the Hui & Gnedin (1997) case-B fit gives 1.4277e-13 cm^3/s at 2e4 K against the 1.43e-13 used here (0.16%), and 2.5918e-13 at 1e4 K against the textbook 2.59e-13 (0.07%). Two temperatures, so the fit is anchored and not just consistent at one point. CASE B, not A: recombinations straight to the ground state are excluded because the photon they emit is reabsorbed on the spot and ionizes another atom, so it is not a net recombination.
checks.name: alpha_B(2e4 K) = 1.43e-13 confirmed by an independent fit

checks.detail: exp(delta) = exp(3.76) = 42.948, which is MD14's 43; evaluating Pawlik's eq. (A1) with (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) = (1.00, -1.71, 0.00, 3.76) against MD14's shorthand agrees to 0.084% at z = 20, 10 and 5.5. So the '43' is not a fitted constant of MD14's: it is e^delta from Pawlik's Table A1, and the clumping factor used here is specifically C_100 -- gas BELOW overdensity 100 -- from the run reheated at z_r = 19.5. Pawlik's C_-1 (all gas) is about twice as large at z = 6, so this choice is the LESS demanding one.
checks.name: MD14's '1 + 43 z^-1.71' IS Pawlik+09 eq. (A1) for C_100, r19.5 run

checks.detail: Pawlik+09 Appendix A1 fits C over 6 <= z <= 20. z = 20 sits exactly at the upper edge and z = 10 well inside, so the C_IGM column is on solid ground there. z = 5.5 is BELOW the fitted range: C_IGM(5.5) = 3.330 is an extrapolation, mild (0.5 in z) but real, and it is the only cell of the tables that leaves a source's stated domain. The fixed-C columns are unaffected -- they assume nothing.
checks.name: the clumping fit is used inside its range at z = 20 and 10, OUTSIDE it at z = 5.5

checks.detail: at (1+z)/7 = 1 and C_IGM = 1: t_rec = 3.1487 Gyr against the 3.2 Gyr printed in their eq. (24). Agreement to 1.6%.
checks.name: MD14 eq. (24) 3.2 Gyr normalisation reproduced from our own n_H0

checks.detail: across all nine (z, C) cells, N_req(t_rec) - t_rec/t_H = 1 to 2.2e-16. THAT is what choosing the recombination time as the clock buys: the recombination part of the budget becomes unity everywhere, and the whole (z, C) dependence moves into the amortised initial ionization, t_rec/t_H. In the Hubble-time normalisation it is the other way round -- the '1' is the initial ionization and the recombination term carries all the variation.
checks.name: in t_rec units the recombination term is exactly 1, by construction

checks.detail: at fixed C = 1 the excess N_req - 1 grows by 2.6362 from z = 10 to z = 20 against the matter-domination prediction (21/11)^1.5 = 2.6378, a 0.06% departure -- that residual is Lambda and radiation in the exact Planck-18 H(z), which the power law omits.
checks.name: the exact table obeys the analytic (1+z)^(3/2) law

checks.detail: alpha_B falls with T, so t_rec ~ 1/alpha_B lengthens and the requirement drops as the assumed IGM gets hotter. Between the two values in common use the recombination term changes by 1.815: at z = 10 with C_IGM = 1.838, N_req goes from 2.606 at MD14's 2e4 K to 3.915 at 1e4 K. T is an ASSUMPTION about photoionized gas, not a measurement of this IGM, and it is the second-largest lever after C.
checks.name: the gas temperature is a real knob, and MD14's choice is the milder one

checks.detail: (N_req-1)|C=12 / (N_req-1)|C=1 = 12.0000000000 at z = 10, against the analytic 12. Exact, as eq. (1d) requires.
checks.name: N_req - 1 is exactly linear in the clumping factor
